contributions.headingText: B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma (B-ALL/LBL) with ETV6::RUNX1 fusion is a neoplasm of lymphoblasts of B-cell lineage defined by the presence of rearrangement between ETV6 on chromosome 12p13.2 and RUNX1 on chromosome 21q22.1.
2A70.Y & XH4KA2 Other B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with recurrent genetic abnormalities & B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with t(12;21)(p13;q22); TEL-AML1 (ETV6-RUNX1)

B-ALL and B-LBL represent the same disease. B-ALL always involves the bone marrow and usually also involves the peripheral blood. Extramedullary involvement is common and is by definition the primary site of involvement in B-LBL. For details, see section B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma .

ETV6::RUNX1 is the most common recurrent translocation in childhood B-ALL/LBL, representing approximately 25% of B-ALL/LBL cases diagnosed in patients aged 2–10 years {7604619; 8609706; 8943861; 22580999}. It is extremely rare in adults and infants {29567885; 34461632}.

The ETV6::RUNX1 fusion has been identified in archival blood spots of neonates who go on to develop this leukaemia in childhood, and in as many as 5% of healthy newborns, suggesting that it is an early event necessary but not sufficient for leukaemogenesis {10551495; 29311095}. There is no known specific environmental or immunological trigger {29784935}.

B-ALL/LBL with ETV6::RUNX1 fusion appears to derive from a B-cell progenitor rather than a haematopoietic stem cell {15908956; 26269126}. The ETV6::RUNX1 fusion results in the production of a fusion protein that probably acts in a dominant negative fashion to interfere with the normal function of the transcription factor RUNX1 and other proteins {17237815}. This leukaemia appears to have a unique gene expression signature {12086872}, including a characteristic high RAG1 expression signature {33987955} and high levels of expression of IGF2BP3 {33805930}; abnormalities of the intact ETV6 allele {9305598}; and PAX5, JAK/STAT pathway, EPOR, and DNA methylation abnormalities {21628403; 22531296; 26269126; 29029492}.

There are no unique features.

Immunophenotyping

Negative or partially positive CD9, CD20, and CD66c appear relatively specific for this subtype {9823952; 10914546; 12094248}. A CD27-positive, CD44-low-to-negative immunophenotype is seen in B-ALL/LBL with ETV6::RUNX1 fusion, as well as in B-ALL/LBL with ETV6::RUNX1-like features {15759032; 30730614}. Myeloid-associated antigens, especially CD13 and CD33, are frequently expressed {9359509; 32368831; 28187514}.

The ETV6::RUNX1 fusion is identifiable by FISH, RT-PCR, and RNA sequencing methods {32150610} and not readily identifiable by standard cytogenetics. Derivative chromosomes and other non-prognostic karyotypic changes may be present {17215856}. Co-occurrence of other recurrent genetic abnormalities in B-ALL/LBL is rare {27895713; 23491079; 29296806}.
Essential: meets the diagnostic criteria for B-ALL/LBL (see section B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma); demonstration of ETV6::RUNX1 fusion.

B-ALL/LBL with ETV6::RUNX1 fusion has a very favourable prognosis, in part due to chemosensitivity {15217836}. Age, presenting white blood cell count, and measurable residual disease after induction chemotherapy are important prognostic factors, but this entity may still have better outcomes than other B-ALL/LBL types with these adverse factors {33739852; 34250504}. Relapses often occur later than do those of other types of B-ALL/LBL. It has been suggested that some late relapses derive from persistent preleukaemic clones that harbour the translocation and undergo additional genetic events after the first leukaemic clone has been eliminated {11468150}. Derivative chromosomes by karyotype do not appear to alter the prognosis. Patients with relapsed B-ALL/LBL with ETV6::RUNX1 fusion have a considerable chance of rescue.
